HOTELS & RESTAURANTS, "The Night Log": one night at the visitor's own hotel, drawn as a lit architectural section in champagne ink on forest; scroll (or turn the lantern's hour ring) from 18:00 to 07:45; Amariya is a gimballed champagne lantern whose liquid stays level while you turn it, lights each room she answers in, rebuilds the house as you describe it, leaves a morning handover on the desk and hangs 30 founding keys at dawn. CLINICS, "The Line": one steel hairline runs the whole page and is the clinical boundary (hers on the left, your team on the right), the phone line and the only line in the design; a frosted porcelain orb lit by the visitor's real sun rolls along it, turns like a dial, can be dropped on anything to ask about it, cannot cross the line (pushing it hands a slip to your team) and turns over to show its edition mark. DENTAL, "First Available": the practice's own day sheet, opened at the visitor's real time and ruled in rose-gold; a nacre pearl rolls down the phone column from call to call, sets a pearl in every gap, and can be lifted and dropped into any open slot to hear the call that fills it. Every previous feature (voice and text with Amariya, dock, live-time story, greetings, profile + live ROI, feature spotlight, scripted calls, polite agent navigation, FAQ, footer, switcher) survives in each concept, plus the founders' offer, honest ledger, guarantee, two-step application and pluggable HubSpot booking. Nine build packages: a foundation (engine + contracts), content, voice UI, then a 3D and a UI package per niche, built in parallel.

=== HOTELS & RESTAURANTS · "The Night Log" (/hotels, theme hospitality, Cormorant Garamond + Supreme, Ranade wordmark)

Experience, chapter by chapter (section id · hour · agent section · feature):

Turn the glass and the champagne stays level, sloshes, fizzes when shaken; tap it and she answers; its light physically falls on the room she is in and swells with her syllables; the whole house behind it is refracted through the glass, and in the lobby the guest's words change language as they pass behind it.

NAVIGATION: hotels = a time dial (the lantern's hour ring, docked in the cornice as the Night Dial; a Night index dialog; hash #h-HHMM); clinics = a line index minimap on the right edge plus ten numbered landmark rings on the line, the orb's ↑/↓ keys jump point to point; dental = a sticky hour ruler on the left that is the scrollbar (only hours with entries get labels) plus a right-edge "Book your call" tab.
LAYOUT GRID: hotels = 12 columns, house in 1–8, a 440px log column in 9–12 over a 92% forest scrim, hour numerals hanging into the log column, annotation leader lines (desktop); clinics = one porcelain sheet split by the line at a different x per chapter (.58/.50/.62/.66/.34/.46/.58/.50/.50), no cards, hairline rules and mono labels; dental = a 96px ruler + 12-column sheet, chairs in columns 1–7 as hatched busy bands, the phone lane in 8–12, rows separated by 1px rose-gold rules, blind-embossed recesses.
SCROLL PARADIGM: hotels = time-scrub: scroll is the clock of one night, a camera rides one rail through the section, each chapter has ten beats; clinics = native scroll with two sticky pins (story, dial), the line S-bends between chapters and the orb rolls along it to the next anchor; dental = scrub through a day on one sheet, one pinned scene (07:45), everything else triggers on the reading line (38svh) and the pearl travels between recesses.
TYPOGRAPHY: hotels = Cormorant Garamond 500/600 display with lining tabular numerals for hours (168/120/88px), Supreme body, running heads in 11px capitals, letterpress stamps; clinics = Newsreader Light 300 display (H1 96px), Newsreader 400 for Amariya's own words (her voice is always the serif), Geist Mono for every label, time, stamp and data point; dental = Instrument Serif 400 display only (h1 64, chapter times, tally figures in fixed-width digit cells, the embossed time numeral up to 18rem), Supreme small caps labels, tabular numerals everywhere.
MOTION LANGUAGE: hotels = light and liquid (cubic-bezier(.45,0,.2,1), 900–1600 ms, springs for the glass), mechanical detents and letterpress stamps (cubic-bezier(.34,1.32,.64,1), 180–320 ms, 3–4% overshoot), text present from first paint with one gilt sweep; clinics = calm clinical precision: only physical things move (orb, line, slips, light), headings are "printed" (a hairline draws under them), numbers roll like a monitor readout, no rising text; dental = ink-in: every entry appears as a left-to-right clip-path wipe at 900px/s with its baseline rule drawing 80 ms ahead, pearl physics (bowl spring, set spring, friction), nothing fades up.
ORB ROLE: hotels = the lantern is the scene's only warm light, the talk button, and (through its ring) the page's clock; clinics = the orb is a pointer (drop it on anything to ask), a dial, a playhead, proof of scope (cannot cross the line) and provenance (the mark on its base); dental = the pearl is the progress marker down the day, the agent's pointer, and a token you place into gaps.
INTERACTION TWIST: hotels = turn the glass and the liquid stays level (gimbal), shake to fizz, tap to ring, turn the ring to turn the night; clinics = push it against the line and it hands off instead of crossing; hold to grip and roll it under your palm to read the mark; dental = long-press to lift it out of its cradle and drop it into a slot; a slow circular rub polishes it to a mirror; the phone line becomes a string that vibrates with her voice.
SHARED UNDERNEATH (one engine): OrbStage + OrbInput (drag-to-spin with inertia, pitch spring, hover tilt, keyboard, touch with pan-y, tap/long-press/carry events), scheduler, scroll/navigator, motion prefs (Pause + reduced), clock, voice bridge + ElevenLabs session + tools, scripted-call player, text typing helpers, ROI/apply/qualify/adapter, analytics, sound.

TAKEN. Hotels: the judge's spine (Night Log) with the grafts (gimballed glass, hour ring as crown/Night Dial, translation through the glass, scenario chips, "Welcome back", telephone-message slip, Do-Not-Disturb hanger, GM handover, honest minutes, etched monogram). Clinics: The Line spine with the editor's light (sundial, night pool), provenance mark, frost-as-privacy and contrast guard, and the auteur's 7-day Course, results report, consent statements and "take the notes". Dental: the day-sheet spine with the editor's print craft (emboss, cradle/bowl physics, live string, practice-type selector, 7-day rule) and the inventor's polish, shape-coded seats, "What she never does", insurance and knocked-out-tooth calls, qualifying question.
CUT OR SIMPLIFIED (engineering, to make nine parallel packages buildable in one pass without sacrificing the concept): (1) Hotels analytic glass renderer: cut; the proven MeshPhysical transmission from champagne.ts is kept and now refracts the real house behind it because house and lantern share ONE WebGL context (the hotels canvas is the page background). (2) Hotels bail-carry, lift doors, blurred reveals, five archetype meshes, stars/headlights and the baked brass-plate normal map: cut (the footer plate is CSS emboss; stars/headlights are a stretch item). (3) Ring FLIP docking: replaced by two instances of the same SVG ring component (one around the glass, one in the cornice) driven by the same NightClock. (4) Clinics spot plate and dental set pearls / string tube: DOM, SVG and CSS instead of extra WebGL views; the light pages keep exactly one WebGL object (the orb) in a fixed canvas, which also keeps the 6 GB test machine and SwiftShader runs feasible. Dental set pearls are CSS pearls born with a sheen flash. (5) Gesture grammar unified so the existing orb tests and the shared input keep working everywhere: plain drag always TURNS the orb (gain 1.6 rad per radius, inertia τ 1.1 s, pitch spring); tap = talk; long-press (350 ms, < 6 px) = LIFT/CARRY (clinics drop-to-ask, dental drop-to-fill); keyboard mirrors every gesture. The spec's "drag = carry by default" (clinics) and "drag translates in the bowl" (dental) become: carry needs the long press; the dental bowl is a 0–.25R visual lean added on top of rolling. (6) No GSAP ScrollTrigger: one scroll owner (Lenis on fine pointers, native otherwise) and sectionProgress() from cached offsets drive every pin and timeline; GSAP core only. (7) HubSpot: the embed, the Forms API and counts are behind one adapter with env-driven IDs; until they exist the page shows an honest "we'll email you a time" line and local storage keeps the record. (8) Audio recordings: never faked; play buttons render only when content declares audio files. (9) All owner-unconfirmed claims (PMS names, "no OTA commission", overage rate, privacy/recording wording, restaurant and physician ROI constants, legal links, reply times, why-30 wording) are typed Pending slots that render nothing. (10) Per-niche OG images and PNG icons are produced by the lead after the first build (puppeteer in the scratchpad), not fabricated by hand. (11) '/' becomes a small brand front door with three doors, not the preview hub.

Expose stop/setMuted/sendText/sendActivity/contextUpdate. Track events: call_started, mic_denied, fell_back_to_text, call_ended.
level.ts: a scheduler job (order 50) that runs only while a conversation exists and motion allows: level = state speaking ? getOutputVolume() : (listening && !muted) ? getInputVolume() : 0; smooth with attack 40 ms / release 200 ms (dt-based), gain 2.2 clamp 1; writes voice.level and :root --amp. packages.title: Hotels 3D: the house world, the gimballed champagne lantern, camera rail, key rack, translation plate
packages.instructions:
Build ONE three.js scene for /hotels rendered by OrbStage in fixed mode with fullFrame: true (the canvas is the page background; alpha false; clear colour var bg-page from colors.ts). Everything in the scene is lit by shader terms, no three.js lights, except brass/glass which use the RoomEnvironment PMREM already used in champagne.ts. Budget: ≤ 30 draw calls, ≤ 80k triangles, DPR cap from the stage, transmissionResolutionScale .5 (.35 coarse), degrade(): .35 and halve bubbles.

index.ts: `createScene(root)` builds the scene from the parts below and exposes `window.amariyaNight` and `window.amariyaHouse` (types.ts: NightApi { minutes; setMinutes(m, o?: {immediate?: boolean}); chapterAt(m); chapters: ChapterInfo[]; on(cb) } and HouseApi { rebuild(p: HouseParams); params; lightRoom(room); carry?: never }). It reads chapters from `section[data-chapter][data-hour]` (hour 'HH:MM', minutes since 18:00 = 0–825; the prologue has data-hour='now' and maps to the visitor's real hour clamped into the night, else 18:00), caches each section's offsetTop/height on ResizeObserver(document.body)+fonts.ready+resize, and maps scroll.y ⇄ minutes piecewise-linearly (director.ts NightClock). setMinutes(m) → scroll.to(y, {immediate}) (used by the ring).
director.ts: scheduler job order 10: read scroll.y once → minutes → chapter + local progress p (10 beats as in CONCEPTS) → camera pose (poses.ts: a pose per data-room: position/target/fov; interpolate on an S-curve over the last 30 % of each chapter; smoothing τ 120 ms; phones FOV 30 instead of 22) → lantern target (the room's desk/window position, radius per chapter: prologue R = min(19svh, 38vw) px, travelling 36–48 px, lobby min(30svh, 34vw), handover 80 px, footer 64 px; a critically damped spring ω 5 rad/s toward the target, banking ≤ .12 rad) → sky by minutes → window occupancy → writes :root --t, --gx/--gy, --ox/--oy/--or and positions the .orb root: root.style.transform = translate(ox−or, oy−or) with width/height = 2·or via --orb (the root is position: fixed, top/left 0; set these in your module at mount: root.style.position='fixed'); below a projected radius of 22 px set root tabindex −1 and pointer-events none (the dock carries Ring) and restore above. Under reduced motion/pause: no springs; jump to the chapter's settled pose and call stage.still() on scroll (the stage already redraws stills on scroll).
sky.ts: a backdrop plane behind the house graded by --t: dusk (sky-dusk) → night (bg-page) → dawn (dawn role mixed in from t > .88); a distant city line of instanced window quads (≤ 400) warm-dim; ~300 star points shown 23:00–04:30 (cheap; skip on coarse pointers).
generator.ts: parametric section kit: HouseParams { floors 2–9 (ceil(rooms/14) clamped), bays 3–12, ground: 'lobby+restaurant'|'restaurant'|'lobby', roof: 'terrace'|'garden'|'plain'|'pitched', name: string }, presets for the four scenarios. Geometry merged with BufferGeometryUtils.mergeGeometries: slabs, side walls, cut faces with a poché ShaderMaterial (house-poche fill, 45° hatch step(.5, fract((x+y)·density)) in house-hatch, blue-noise 3 % grain), rooms as an InstancedMesh of unit planes with per-instance atlas offsets (atlas.ts draws a 1024² Canvas2D silhouette atlas: bed, table+chairs, lamp, cloche, flute, phone with an emissive LED dot), windows as one InstancedMesh (≤ 220; attributes aLit, aOcc, aSeed; filament flicker 0→.6 in 80 ms, →.4 in 60 ms, →1 in 500 ms when lit changes; occupancy by hour: ~40 % evening, 12 % 02–05, dusk by day), every edge merged into one LineSegments whose shader fades with depth and brightens near uLantern (house-line → house-line-lit), a canopy name plane (CanvasTexture, Cormorant 600, redrawn only on name change), a lift shaft and a roof per type. rebuild(p) ≤ 8 ms, debounced 150 ms, new house rises through a uRise clip over 900 ms with a 1 px gold seam; data-room → world anchor map exported for the director (restaurant, lobby, room214 (top floor right), desk, office (ground back), room507 (fifth floor), handover (desk), keys (rack behind the desk), checkout (street)). Lighting term in all house shaders: warmth·max(n·l,0)/(1 + d²·6)·(1 + .35·amp) from uLantern/uWarm/uAmp, plus window glow and a dawn directional from --t. Clamp output luminance behind the log column (uScrimX in NDC) to ≤ bg-page lightened 8 %.
lantern.ts + liquid.ts: group = glass sphere (MeshPhysicalMaterial from champagne.ts: transmission 1, ior 1.5, thickness 1.4, roughness .06, clearcoat, dispersion .3 desktop only, attenuation champagne; etched band + 'A' monogram via a roughness CanvasTexture so rotation reads), the liquid: a second sphere (r .96) MeshPhysicalMaterial (lantern colour, transmission .6, ior 1.34, attenuation (σ ≈ .9,1.3,3.2)) clipped by a world-space clippingPlane whose normal is world-up tilted by the slosh angle α and whose constant is the fill level (56 % idle), side DoubleSide, plus a thin emissive meniscus disc mesh aligned to the plane (brass-hi, additive); bubbles: THREE.Points (600 / 220 coarse) rising from three nucleation points fixed in the glass frame (vertex shader: world-up rise .18–.32 R/s, grow 1→1.7×, discard above the plane), rate 24/s + 200/s·|ω|; gold flecks (300) Brownian below the surface; gimbal: brass torus ring (metalness 1, roughness .3) with two pins and a bail (half torus) — brass lit by the PMREM; glow: one additive halo sprite (no bloom). Physics (liquid.ts, 120 Hz substeps from input.step cadence): glass yaw/pitch from the stage frame (yaw unlimited, pitch from the input spring); self-righting roll 0; liquid tilt α: damped oscillator ωn 6.9, ζ .14, forced by the glass's angular acceleration (−.02·dω/dt) and scroll velocity (pitch rate −v·.0006 clamped ±.6 rad/s), capped ±.42; spin follows yaw rate τ .42 s, decays τ 1.8 s, vortex depth .022·ω²·R ≤ .16R (dip the plane centre via a radial displacement in the liquid vertex shader); voice states: connecting = fill 40 → 58 % over 1.2 s + bead chain; listening = mirror-still surface, inward rings amplitude .012R·amp, bubbles 3/s, core −25 % cooler; thinking = spin 1.4 rad/s vortex, candle flicker ±4 %; speaking = bubbles 24 + 300·amp, outward rings ≤ 6/s, core .7 + amp, room light ×(1 + .35·amp); muted = frost ring at the meniscus (uniform); tone: bright ×1.4 bubbles +15 % core, soft ×.85 −15 %, calm paler, warm default; hover within 1.6R leans ≤ .12 rad to the cursor (τ 250 ms), core +12 %, cursor circulation adds spin (+.15·Γ, cap 1.6 rad/s). The lantern is the only warm light: pass its world position/warmth to every house shader.
keys.ts: in chapter #keys only: a wooden board plane, 30 hooks, one InstancedMesh key (bow torus + blade box + fob, ~400 tris, brass PMREM; matcap on coarse), fob numbers from a 512² atlas; per-key damped pendulum θ'' = −81.7·sinθ − 1.6·θ'; cursor velocity within 120 px pushes nearby keys; ledger states from content/ledgerCounts: issued → key removed + engraved plate, held → tinted champagne-700 fob, open → hangs. API window.amariyaKeys { swing(n), lift(n), setLedger({issued, held}) } (lift = the next open key rises 6 cm and turns to face the camera).
translation.ts: a text plane (Canvas2D, Supreme 400, lantern colour on transparent) positioned behind the glass in the lobby chapter, showing pairs from `ul[data-translations] li` (each li: data-src text, data-lang target text); the source sentence slides right-to-left behind the upper 44 % of the globe every 4.5 s; the DOM sentence is masked by P4; the plate is only in the lobby chapter. Dawn (t > .88): windows go out in seeded order over 4 s, the lantern pales to lantern/ivory, a raking sunrise crosses the facade. Per-chapter culling: rack only in #keys, plate only in #lobby, city/stars by time. Dispose everything. Provide a 'lights down' hook: window.amariyaNight.jump(minutes) = setMinutes immediate (the DOM scrim is P4's). Type-check with tsc; syntax-check with rolldown.
acceptance: On /hotels the fixed canvas shows the house section with lit windows matching the visitor's hour; the lantern sits in the lobby at R = min(19svh, 38vw) and .orb.is-live is set within 25 s under SwiftShader

Scrolling moves the camera along the rail and the lantern between rooms in order: restaurant, lobby (close-up), room 214, night desk, back office, room 507, desk (handover), key rack, street; :root --t goes 0→1 and --ox/--oy/--or track the lantern (verified by reading the CSS vars at five scroll positions)
Turning the glass (drag) keeps the liquid surface level and sloshing; a throw fizzes (bubble rate rises); the orb tests (dragtest.mjs) pass unchanged
setState('listening') stills the surface and gathers flecks; setState('speaking') with amp .85 raises bubble rate and brightens the occupied room (pixel luminance of the room increases)
window.amariyaHouse.rebuild({floors:7, bays:5, ground:'lobby+restaurant', roof:'terrace', name:'The Harbour House'}) rebuilds within one frame of the 150 ms debounce, the name appears on the canopy
window.amariyaNight.setMinutes(348) scrolls the page to the 23:48 chapter; chapterAt() returns ids in order
Key rack draws only in #keys; amariyaKeys.swing(7) swings key 07; ledger states render by shape
Reduced motion and Pause: a still per chapter, redrawn on scroll; no bubbles or slosh
No per-frame getBoundingClientRect except the stage's one read; draw calls ≤ 30 (renderer.info.render.calls logged once in dev)

physics.ts (120 Hz substeps): CRADLE: plain drag turns the pearl through OrbInput (unchanged) and additionally leans the root toward the drag by min(.25R, .3·drag) with a bowl spring return (k 9 ζ .7, rolling friction τ .9 s) — so the pearl visibly rolls in its recess and springs back; a throw (release velocity) rolls it up to .5R and back. POLISH: a slow circular rub (radius ≤ .3R, speed ≤ 2R/s, held ≥ 400 ms, detected from pointermove samples on the root) ramps lustre 0→1 over 600 ms (uLustre/uPatch from the pointer direction through the inverse group quaternion), decays exp(−dt/8 s) after the hand leaves; keyboard P held polishes the facing patch. LIFT/CARRY: on 'orb:longpress' lift (scale 1.04, shadow widens/softens, sound 'hush' off by default), on 'orb:carrymove' follow the pointer along the lane axis (x locked to the lane centre ± 24 px; y free), open recesses within reach ([data-slot][data-open]) get data-reach for P8's fill, dragging within 80 px of the viewport's top/bottom edge auto-scrolls at ≤ 600 px/s (scroll.to relative, immediate); on 'orb:drop' within 40 px of an open recess SET it: critically damped spring to the slot centre (k 28, ~350 ms), a 6 px dip, sound 'tink', dispatch 'sheet:fill' {slot: id} on document and voice.contextUpdate('The visitor dropped Amariya into the {time} gap'); elsewhere roll back to the nearest slot with friction. SCROLL: the pearl is pinned at the reading line (38svh) while the sheet moves: rotation.x += Δy/R so it rolls over still paper; between entries it travels to the next recess with τ 200 ms and settles with the bowl spring; the active slot = the last [data-slot][data-anchor] whose page top ≤ scroll.y + .38·innerHeight (cached offsets); dispatch 'pearl:arrive' {slot} on change. risks_and_mitigations:
1. Parallel packages drift from the contracts (prop names, events, attributes). Mitigation: contracts are explicit and the P0 stubs already carry the final markup hooks; the Integrate phase has a checklist (section 5 of the test plan) and may edit any file.
2. Hotels one-context scene is the heaviest; SwiftShader test runs are slow. Mitigation: transmission at .5/.35, per-chapter culling, the stage's one-time degrade, 25 s is-live timeouts; if still too slow in CI, the lead lowers DPR cap to 1 for hotels in boot (a one-line change).
3. TypeScript is not checked by astro build. Mitigation: typescript 5.9.3 added; every package runs `npx tsc --noEmit`.
4. ElevenLabs allowlist does not include 127.0.0.1/localhost:4321 or the Vercel preview host → sessions fail. Mitigation: a plain toast and text fallback; owner action listed in open questions; tests use simulate().
5. The stage's fixed-canvas scissor clearing leaves ghosts when the view moves fast. Mitigation: clear the union of the previous and current view each frame; the Integrate phase screenshots while scrolling.
6. Clinics line geometry breaks on content growth (details opening, errors). Mitigation: ResizeObserver(main) recompute debounced 100 ms; straight-line fallback for a segment that no longer fits.
7. Dental long-press lift vs scrolling on touch. Mitigation: pan-y everywhere, lift only after 350 ms without movement, carry sets touch-action none and preventDefault only then; a plain swipe always scrolls; the drop zones also work by tap and keyboard.
8. Contrast over live 3D. Mitigation: text only on the hotels scrim (92 %) or solid surfaces, shader luminance clamp behind the log column, the clinics shadow alpha cap .16 with a generator pair, and rendered-pixel sampling in the test plan.
9. Memory/disk on the build machine. Mitigation: no new heavy dependencies, no Playwright, one browser at a time, idle-loaded three in its own chunk, textures ≤ 20 MB.
10. Owner-unconfirmed content shipping by accident. Mitigation: Pending<T> slots render nothing and are listed in the open questions; the content package must not invent values.
11. HubSpot IDs missing. Mitigation: adapter + meetingsUrl() return null → honest copy; the whole funnel works locally.
12. The old agent prompt still books 'demos' and quotes $299/$799. Mitigation: the page accepts the old tool keys and maps them to the founding licence; the prompt/tool update in the ElevenLabs dashboard is an owner action in the same release.
open_questions_for_user: HubSpot: the meetings embed links per niche (PUBLIC_HUBSPOT_MEETINGS_HOTELS/CLINICS/DENTAL) and, later, the Forms/pipeline IDs for the server route; until then applications are stored locally and the page says 'We'll be in touch by email'.
